messages:
ana: Quick report from onboarding: brought up nova-12b with int4v2-pack and a 45k streaming prefill. Repro: deterministic checksum split vs oracle starting at token 19968. Not seeing randomness across runs.

ryan: can you paste the command and a minimal repro? which pack mode / stride?

ana: repro:```
./onboard.sh --model nova-12b --quant int4v2-pack --context 46080 --prefill streaming --prefill-stride=6144 --seed=11 --kv-debug=trace
```
Log:```
[2026-03-30 14:02:11] prefill.streaming.len=46080 stride=6144
[2026-03-30 14:03:02] kv.checksum(oracle)=0xf1e2d3c4
[2026-03-30 14:03:02] kv.checksum(live)=0xf1e2d33a  <-- divergence @ token 19968
```
This token window contains a mix of prose + an indented markdown block (code fenced).

leah: 19968 is odd but equals 3 * 6144 + 5376; could be an interaction between stride/chunk tail handling and our new phase_taper interpolation. Did you capture ropestate and pack dumps?

ana: uploaded artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/eng-ml/nova/221 (ropestate.log, pack-tail-dump.bin, kvsync.trace). ropestate.phase_taper shows a tiny offset (~2 units) immediately after a pack-tail write.

mira: hypothesis: int4v2-pack vectorized tail path uses a conditional memcpy for nibble-alignment that, under certain tail sizes, misorders the phase accumulator update vs the KV write completion. That would cause live to resume with a stale phase_accum. Try PREFILL_CHUNK_ALIGN=4096 and PACK_TAIL_FALLBACK=scalar to force scalar tail path.

ryan: also run with ROPE_TAPER=off and ROPE_TAPER=aggressive to see if taper interpolation changes where drift occurs. If taper mode moves or eliminates split then rescale timing is likely involved.

ana: kicking quick CI: 1) PACK_TAIL_FALLBACK=scalar, 2) PREFILL_CHUNK_ALIGN=4096, 3) ROPE_TAPER=off. infra-bot queued.

infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17780 (pack-tail-scalar)
infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17781 (chunk-align-4096)
infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17782 (rope-taper-off)

leah: if those don't fix it, next isolate by running single-shard with ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=0 and ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=1 to see if ordering vs asynchrony matters. Also try FP16-only binary to rule out packing math.

ana: will add those. One more quick local test: I ran with KV_GUARDBAND=1 (extra copy-on-write buffer) and saw the split move a few tokens later, which hints at a memcopy tail race. Posting byte-level diffs of pack-tail dump in the artifact.

ryan: great. If pack-tail scalar fixes it, plan a patch to make scalar tail the default until we can audit the vector tail memcpy under diff alignment. If FP16 passes, then it's almost certainly pack/quant path.

mira: agreed. also add a unit test that replays first 20.5k tokens and asserts checksum equality between oracle and live; that'll speed bisecting.

ana: added unit test to repo/tests/kv_prefill/test_tail_repro.py and started local run. Will update with CI links and diffs in ~30m. :hourglass:
